body: I think this is not a bug, as it is intended to obtain the actual bone index of the Skeleton through skin's mapping.

> I think this is not a bug, as it is intended to obtain the actual bone index of the Skeleton through skin's mapping.

Please could you explain this further, as I'm unsure if maybe you mean one of the following or something different?

1) Do you mean you believe the code that returns the surface arrays is working as intended as it's getting the bone indices from the structure of the original imported file (e.g. the fbx etc. file) and this is what you mean by the skins' mapping?  
(though in my case those indices are identical to the Skeleton3D nodes hierarchy so should still match).

2) That there's some internal process on import of the skinned mesh which is different to the Skeleton3Ds hierarchy?

3) That there's a further method/function that needs to be used to get the matching bone name to the surface arrays bone indices through some GDScript function from the bound skin or skin asset? (and if so, do you know what it is?)

Or none of the above and I've misinterpreted what you meant entirely.

Either way, I do still feel that whether this is intended behaviour or not, that most users would expect the bone indices to match the original skeleton.

The Skeleton and MeshInstance/Skin are independent objects, and their indices are not guaranteed to match. So the statement "3" may be similar.

We omitted the commit for stability, but there is a function mapping the skeleton's bone and skin's bone indices within the code I wrote previously for modifying the Skin during Bone processing. I assume you can refer `BoneExpander3D::_map_skin()` in `bone_expander_3d.cpp` to that:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/a53b1017d44ea20c349c5cfddf0c731f0e6132b4..17b63ce169816d0be4fa7fbb522d75e33724cd57#diff-63686fe2d21ee13012ae585d5a71d6fa798b15e6451932bcae29f1ea9014c321L270

(BTW, regarding stability issues, these stem is not related with indexing problems and from the ambiguity of Skeleton and Skin ownership, which leads to performance degradation and complicates initialization timing.)
